summary: This incident report reviews major blackouts from September 2023 through 2029 in New York, Texas, Paris/London, India, South America, California and Japan. It draws lessons from each, such as smart grids, weatherization, cross-border policy reform, renewables, cybersecurity, distributed energy resources and storage. It concludes that AI, blockchain and other emerging technologies could make large-scale blackouts historical anecdotes.
one_line: Report on major blackouts from 2023 to 2029 and the technology lessons, from smart grids to AI and storage, that followed.
key_facts: On September 12, 2023, New York suffered a blackout lasting hours, triggered by a substation failure on the Upper East Side that cascaded through the network.
After the New York blackout, investments went into smart grid technologies, including advanced sensors and automation systems for real-time analysis and rapid response.
In February 2024, unprecedented cold caused a surge in electricity demand and widespread power plant failures in Texas.
Texas responses included enhanced weather forecasting models, grid automation, and decentralized resources such as battery storage and microgrids.
On June 5, 2025, a fault in the UK-France interconnection grid caused a simultaneous outage in Paris and London affecting millions.
European nations reinvented cross-border energy policies and funded a pan-European grid incorporating blockchain for secure energy transactions.
In July 2026, a heatwave overloaded India's national grid, causing a blackout affecting nearly half a billion people.
India's response was to accelerate renewable deployment, including solar and wind farms with intelligent demand-prediction software, and energy storage systems.
In 2027, coordinated cyberattacks left millions in South America without power for days; blockchain ledgers were later integrated into grid operations to secure energy transactions.
The California brownouts of 2028 showed the value of distributed energy resources such as home solar panels and neighborhood battery systems.
Rolling blackouts in Japan in autumn 2029 prompted a nationwide push for large-scale storage such as lithium-ion batteries and pumped hydro.
Utilities worldwide are testing AI-driven platforms that manage energy flow, perform predictive maintenance, and self-heal by rerouting power during outages.
